axisScale.meaning: Corpus-relative axis position; higher is always more desirable. 50 is typical across measured sources. Each axis keeps its adjusted z-score in the z field, while the display score applies one shared corpus calibration across all axes so positions remain comparable.
axisScale.method: adjusted z-score scaled by the pooled 95th percentile absolute z position across all measured axes and sources, then bounded to 0–100

compositeScale.meaning: Corpus-relative measured headline value. 50 is typical across measured sources; higher indicates more concrete headline information and less attention packaging after comparison with similar story mixes.
compositeScale.method: natural-unit axis residuals, empirically shrunk for sample size, symmetrically saturated at a corpus-derived high-percentile axis deviation, averaged across the eleven composite axes, then centred and scaled across eligible sources

bands.label: Strongest measured headline value
bands.summary: Headlines most often combine concrete information with comparatively restrained packaging.

bands.label: Above-typical measured headline value
bands.summary: Headlines are usually informative or restrained, with some weaker axes or mixed behaviour.

bands.label: Below-typical measured headline value
bands.summary: Headlines more often omit concrete anchors or use more attention-oriented framing.

bands.label: Weakest measured headline value
bands.summary: Headlines are comparatively thin on concrete information, heavier on packaging, or both.

axes.label: Events & actions
axes.description: The headline says something happened, changed or was decided; speech acts and noun-led event references count less than direct action verbs.

axes.label: Numbers & detail
axes.description: The headline carries concrete quantities, amounts, ages or counts; bare years and scale words count less, while product/listicle numerals are discounted.

axes.label: Time & place
axes.description: The headline anchors the story in a time or location; place candidates are precision-filtered because headline-case entity recognition often mistakes teams, brands and products for places.

axes.label: Cause & effect
axes.description: The headline links events, causes or consequences.

axes.label: Real-world stakes
axes.description: The headline signals costs, risks, harm, benefit or other material consequences.

axes.label: Evidence cues
axes.description: The headline points to evidence surface: documents/data/legal material strongest, typed research next, direct testimony or quotation moderate, and vague sourcing weak.

axes.label: Context & comparison
axes.description: The headline compares, contrasts or places events in a sequence; bare sequence markers count less than explicit comparisons or historical anchors.

axes.label: Explanatory framing
axes.description: The headline offers explanation, mechanism, guidance or service information.

axes.label: Curiosity restraint
axes.description: The headline resolves rather than withholds the central example, reason, mechanism, timing or referent; stock teasers count most strongly.

axes.label: Low search-capture packaging
axes.description: The headline avoids direct-address, how-to and search-capture packaging.

axes.label: Sensational restraint
axes.description: The headline avoids sensational vocabulary and celebrity/personal-life framing.
